narrative:
The model determined that you have a 95% chance of failing the bar exam on your first attempt. Because the law school sets a high bar for admission, this strong prediction of failure led directly to the rejection of your application.

Three factors drove this outcome, ranked by importance. Your third-year class ranking had the greatest influence. Placing in the first decile—far below the average of nearly sixth decile among accepted students—strongly pushed the prediction toward failure. Your first-year ranking in the second decile, also well below the typical sixth-decile level of accepted applicants, added further weight in the same direction. Finally, your family income bracket of Middle contributed additional influence toward failure, though it was the least powerful of the three.

Taken together, these academic performance signals and background factor created a clear picture for the model: a high likelihood that the bar exam would prove difficult on the first try.

You should focus on strengthening your academic record and bar-exam readiness. Consider retaking key courses to raise your class standing, enrolling in a structured bar-preparation program, and seeking mentorship from recent graduates who succeeded on their first attempt. With targeted improvement in these areas, you can materially change your prospects for future applications. (218 words)
